# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 20 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 20
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. It is therefore good that one who has learned the righteous ordinances of the Lord, as many as are written, should walk in them. For whoever does these things will be glorified in the kingdom of God; and whoever chooses the opposite will perish along with his works.
2. For this reason there is a resurrection; for this reason there is a retribution.
3. I beseech those who occupy positions of honor — if you have received any counsel of good will, do not put away any from among you, but love them all the more and strive even harder for their salvation.

---

## Council Notes

- v.1: The conclusion of the Two Ways teaching (chapters 18-20): the two paths lead to two outcomes — glorification in God's kingdom or perishing with one's works. This is standard Two Ways eschatology.
- v.2: "For this reason there is a resurrection; for this reason there is a retribution" — the Two Ways teaching is grounded in eschatology: the moral choices of this life have eternal consequences. The resurrection and retribution are presented as the logical ground (*dia touto*) of the ethical system, not merely its sanction.
- v.3: The address to "those who occupy positions of honor" (*hoi en timē*) — community leaders are specifically exhorted not to exclude or expel members, but to work harder for those who struggle. This pastoral note echoes chapter 2's auxiliary-of-faith theme.
- Chapter 20 is notably brief; the Greek text is also uncertain in places. It functions as a transitional epilogue between the Two Ways (18-19) and the final letter-closing (21).
